messages.author: d79deff2ac4a4c6a
messages.subject: Date/time format on graphing issue?
parts:
Hello everyone - 

I’m trying to plot a simple graph of current speed over time. My code is as follows:

tides <- read.csv("Currents_July_7G_8444.csv")
names(tides)[4] <- "Direction"
names(tides)[5] <- "WaterSpeed"

dates<- as.POSIXlt(tides$date_time, tz= "Etc/GMT-7", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")

plot(dates, tides$WaterSpeed)

This is the error message I receive:

Error in plot.window(...) : need finite 'xlim' values
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In min(x) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning Inf
2: In max(x) : no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
And here’s a sample of my data:

 latitude..degree. longitude..degree.            date_time Direction WaterSpeed
1           38.0346          -122.1252 2008-07-29T00:01:00Z       313       10.0
2           38.0346          -122.1252 2008-07-29T00:08:00Z       319        9.2
3           38.0346          -122.1252 2008-07-29T00:14:00Z       302       14.5
4           38.0346          -122.1252 2008-07-29T00:20:00Z       335       15.8
5           38.0346          -122.1252 2008-07-29T00:26:00Z         0       19.8
6           38.0346          -122.1252 2008-07-29T00:32:00Z       328       17.9
  sea_water_temperature..C.
1                     19.76
2                     19.77
3                     19.76
4                     19.76
5                     19.76
6                     19.76



Any ideas? I thought maybe it was a date formatting issue (hence the “as.POSIXlt” code), but can’t seem to fix it even if the dates are of this class. 

Thanks!

Alex

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Date/time format on graphing issue?
parts:
Good questions. And what does str(dates) return? Also, what does:

any(is.na(dates))

return.

FWIW, I found the following snippet on the web, and it appears to plot
correctly:

now_lt <- as.POSIXlt(Sys.time(), tz = "GMT")
tm <- seq(0, 600, by = 10)
x <- now_lt - tm
y <- rnorm(length(x))
plot(x, y)

-- Mike

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Date/time format on graphing issue?
parts:
Mike and Alexandra, 

Alex sent me the csv and said that the dates weren't parsing. They were all NAs. I used lubridate and managed to get them to parse. Not sure what you need to do to use as.posix(). 

library(lubridate)

tides <- read.csv("~/Downloads/Currents_July_7G_8444.csv")

dates <- parse_date_time(tides$date_time, tz="Etc/GMT-7", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")

plot(dates, tides$WaterSpeed)



Dates are always a PITA in R. 

Good luck Alex. Interesting data. 

B

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Date/time format on graphing issue?
parts:
Thanks, Brandon.  Speaking of PITA, I wonder what:

    str(tides$date_time)

returns.  IIRC, read.csv will return *factors* by default.  If that's the problem, then:

    read.csv(..., stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

would solve the problem.  (As would: library(readr); read_csv(...) for that matter.)

-- Mike
